main_text.l: Cælo ergo conuenit figura sphærica. In quolibet enim genere
unum & simplex ordine naturæ præcedit multi-
plex & compositum. At sphæra unica includitur
superficie, sicut Circulus una finitur linea. Reliquæ
pluribus. Deinde sphærica figura omnibus suis parti-
bus uergit in sese, & semetipsam concludit ac con-
tinet, Reliquæ omnes ab hac perfectione
gura etiam simplici ac ὁμοιομερεῖ includitur.
enim partes eius inter se sunt simillimæ, at solidarum figu-
bitus habentium, quas ἰσοπερίμετρα uocant, ca-
pacissima est, Circularis inter planas, Sphæra in-
enim corpora omnia circumflexu suo cingit ac complectitur.

page.notes: The Greek words are printed in a Greek type face; "ὁμοιομερὴς" and related forms are read from the scan with some doubt. Initial "QVINTO" and "SEXTO" are set with large initial letters and are treated as headings. The last line "uocan-" is a catchword at the foot right.
